text: The file name carries the version of the family. The next version is v3, its change log starts at 3, and the source is recorded as 2 as the file name and 1 as the version in its own table, both kept in the metadata row 'Source version'.
why: The source file is named v2 and its own table says Version 1; the family has no change log and no earlier file in the folder, so the two numbers cannot both be the surviving version, and the next version has to be named without discarding either number.
read: Rules v1 §R8.2 (the next version is the highest v<n> of the family plus 1, in the same folder); the file name of the source; the source table rows 'Version' and 'Date'; the folder listing of 05 Technical architecture.
applied_in: Metadata table (Version 3, Source version row); change log
confirm: Document control confirms that the file name is the version of the family.
impact: Version 3 is the next version; no number of the source is lost because both are recorded.

text: No recovery point objective and no recovery time objective is set for any store or any service. Every store row and every service statement carries the placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents (CG-B-TECH-11-2; ASM-B-TECH-11-2)'; no tier, no number of minutes and no number of hours is taken from the proposed tiers that Architecture v5 mentions.
why: Version 2 gives 'The ACE value' with the status open, Architecture v5 records 'RPO/RTO: not yet set' and names proposed tiers that exist in no source of this run, and the design may not invent a value that a restore test would then have to meet.
read: v2 section 1 rows 'Recovery point objective' and 'Recovery time objective'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 48 ('RPO/RTO: not yet set' and 'NFR gap: RPO/RTO are not set in NFR Spec v3; proposed tiers'); Temporal and Drools design L1 and slide 27.
applied_in: Section 1.1 (owner rows for the two objectives); section 1.4 (store table and consequences); section 4
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure with Operations and Compliance set the ACE value and the per-store tier before the first production release.
impact: The restore test records the measured time and cannot pass or fail against a target until the value is set; the gap is needed by wave 1 and blocks the non-functional story's Done, not a wave start.

text: Report queries read the rwb-reporting read model built from the events, and neither the 19 live schemas nor a data lake. The scaling bullet is rewritten to say so and keeps its two prohibitions.
why: The target architecture removes the data lake and gives rwb-reporting the read model, so the v2 sentence sends a report query to a store that no longer exists.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 and slide 41 (P9 reporting); Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-17; Ownership Map v1 Jobs sheet (JOB-15 owner P9); ids.json (ADR-018).
confirm: P9 rwb-reporting confirms the read model covers the steering and regulatory reports of version 2.
impact: The reporting path is consistent with the architecture; no report is designed against the removed lake.

text: The seven load rows of version 2 are kept word for word, and the small differences from Architecture v5 (23,600 against 23,570 open cases, 410 against 414 online in the busiest hour, 26,500 against 26,479 at the end of 2027) are read as the same forecast, with the 2031 figure added in the new section 2.1.
why: Both sets of numbers come from the same forecast (Volume and Scale Forecast v3) and differ by under 0.2 percent; changing a published row for a rounding difference would break the fidelity of the version for no engineering benefit.
read: v2 section 2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 33 and 48 and their notes.
confirm: Architecture confirms that both sets are the same forecast at different rounding.
impact: Capacity and load tests use the source rows; the 2031 horizon is available to the sizing work.

text: All 19 services carry the same two availability targets, 99.9 percent in business hours and 99.5 percent outside them excluding the change window, because the only target in any source is a service target and the source defines no tiering.
why: Architecture v5 slide 48 states the target per service and gives no tier; inventing a lower target for a service would invent a value, and inventing a higher one would over-promise.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 48 ('Service targets (NFR v3): 99.9% in business hours'); v2 section 1; Rules v1 §R4 (19 services); ids.json (ADR-013).
confirm: Architecture confirms that the service target applies to all 19 without a tier.
impact: Every service has a measurable target; a later tiering decision would change 19 cells and no design element.

text: The 99.9 percent is a target per service and not per screen. A screen composed from two services sees the product, 99.8 percent, and stays inside the 2 second target through the one-hop budget of 0.15 s gateway and session, 0.6 s slowest parallel call and 0.3 s merge, about 1.2 s.
why: With the module cut into 19 services a composed screen depends on two or more services, and the source states both the per-service target and the composition budget without relating them.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 (the response budget and the parallel calls) and slide 48; ids.json (ADR-020).
confirm: Architecture confirms the reading of the per-service target as a component-level target.
impact: The availability figure of a screen and the per-service figure are not confused in a test or a report.

text: Per-topic sizing reads the one sized topic of Architecture v5, rwb.payment.events.v1, as the default for the other topics: 12 partitions, replication factor 3 and 7 days retention, changed per service by RWB-PLT-EVT.
why: Only one topic is sized in any source, and a table with no sizing at all would leave the platform story with no starting point; the retry topics and the dead-letter topic are stated by the same slide.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 22 ('rwb.payment.events.v1 key caseId - 12 partitions - RF 3 - 7 days'; retry 1 min / 10 min / 1 h then .dlt + alert) and slide 11.
confirm: RWB-PLT-EVT sets the partition count per topic from the measured event rate before wave 1.
impact: The platform story has a default; a per-topic change touches the platform and not the design of a service.

text: The screen composition is owned by RWB-PLT-EDGE (gateway-bff), and the partner gateway row of section 5 is read as RWB-PLT-EDGE with S9 rwb-partner behind it; the map has no component row for either edge.
why: The Ownership Map names neither component and the design needs one owner per row; the platform epic is the owner of the edge in the target structure.
read: Ownership Map v1 sheets Services, Tables, Endpoints and Jobs; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10 and 35; Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.1 (RWB-PLT-EDGE).
confirm: Architecture adds the two edge components to the Ownership Map at its next revision.
impact: The edge has an owner in this document; until the map carries the row, a work package names the epic rather than a service code.

text: 'The recovery module adds no separate service' is read as 'Recovery adds no separate platform': the 19 services run on the ACE cluster with the ACE Kafka, Temporal and database, each as an API deployment of two pods and a worker deployment scaled by KEDA.
why: The v2 sentence was written for one module and would otherwise contradict 19 services, while its meaning in the architecture is that no new platform is introduced.
read: v2 section 3 bullet 1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 5, 33 and 41; Temporal and Drools design L1 and L2; ids.json (ADR-013, ADR-016).
confirm: Architecture confirms the reading of the sentence as a statement about the platform and not about the number of deployables.
impact: The sentence stays recognisable and no new platform is claimed.

text: Per-service detection and alerting are owned by RWB-PLT-OBS, and no threshold, detection time, error budget or on-call arrangement is stated, because no source sets one.
why: ADR-023 makes observability a per-service concern and the source has no monitoring target; a threshold would be an invented value.
read: v2 sections 1, 5 and 6; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 34 and 35; Rules v1 §R5.1 (RWB-PLT-OBS); ids.json (ADR-023).
confirm: RWB-PLT-OBS states the detection and alerting target in the observability specification.
impact: The owner is named and the value stays open; no test is written against an invented threshold.

text: The level 'COLLINS load complete - By 07:00' is owned by P1 rwb-source-data, with P3 rwb-case and P8 rwb-payment named in the same 05:00 to 07:00 chain, and the deadline is not divided per service in this document.
why: The deadline covers four owners and the source gives one number; dividing it would invent four numbers, and leaving it unowned would leave the level untestable.
read: v2 section 1 row 'COLLINS load complete'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 33 and 48; Ownership Map v1 Jobs sheet (JOB-04 P1, JOB-07 P8, JOB-02, JOB-03 and JOB-06 P3).
confirm: The batch and scheduling design divides the deadline per step of the chain.
impact: The level has one accountable owner and the chain is visible; the per-step deadline stays with the scheduling design.

text: The load test stays with RWB-ITG-TE009-ITG (the split of RWB-TE-009); the failover test is owned by RWB-PLT-NF06-DB with the ACE DBA; the restore test by P5 rwb-document with RWB-PLT-DB; the replay gate by each service with RWB-PLT-WF; the contract tests by the CON story of each service; the boundary test by each service with the ACE DBA.
why: Two of the four tests of the source have no story in the split plan, and a test without an owner is not built; the owners are taken from the existing stories and not invented.
read: v2 section 6; split_plan.json (RWB-TE-009 to RWB-ITG-TE009-ITG, NF-06 to RWB-PLT-NF06-DB); Rules v1 §R5.7 (CON stories are Day 1) and §R7.2 s16 (test levels); Temporal and Drools design slide 27 (replay gate E2-040) and Ownership Map v1 Jobs sheet (JOB-21 PLT).
confirm: QA confirms the mapping and whether a separate test story is raised for the failover and the restore drill.
impact: Every test named by the source has a build owner; no test story is invented in this document.
